final_candidates.decision_summary: Lys119 forms the internal PLP aldimine; alanine substitution eliminates Schiff-base formation and fully abolishes catalysis while preserving the fold.
Cys52 is the heme-ligating thiolate in the N-terminal heme domain; removing it disrupts heme binding and severely cripples CBS activity.
His65 is the axial heme ligand; alanine substitution disrupts heme coordination, causing strong loss of function with largely intact fold.

stop_reason.detail: Cofactor-ligand mutations already provide maximal mechanistic loss-of-function confidence; no external evidence available to refine further.

history.rationale: C52 is the verified heme-ligating cysteine (Cys-52/His-65 axial pair in the N-terminal heme domain); removing this ligand disrupts the heme environment tightly coupled to active-site integrity and strongly impairs CBS activity.

Cys52 is the heme-ligating residue in the N-terminal heme-binding domain; removing its thiolate ligand disrupts heme binding and severely cripples CBS activity. WT residue verified as C at position 52.
H65 is the second axial heme ligand verified in the sequence (SESPHHH motif); alanine substitution destabilizes heme binding and reduces catalytic turnover substantially.
His65 is the axial heme ligand; replacing it disrupts heme coordination and abolishes activity while leaving the fold largely intact. WT residue verified as H at position 65.
Lys119 forms the internal aldimine with the PLP cofactor; mutating it to Ala eliminates Schiff-base formation and fully abolishes catalysis. WT residue verified as K at position 119 in the sequence.
Mutation of this conserved active-site cysteine pair is a classic severe loss-of-function mechanism in CBS. WT residue verified as C at position 244.
